verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input to this arithmetic is published and none of it is obscure. The $388-406m FY27 range is not a June disclosure at all -- it was set on 2026-04-07 as an explicit TDS-only outlook against FY26 TDS revenue of $403.7m stated in the same 8-K, so 'the guide brackets flat on continuing revenue' was on the tape the day it was issued and the stock fell 12.02% that day. Q1 at $94.5m / -4.7%, the government-bookings softness and the 21% consumer decline are all in the 2026-06-09 release and call, on which the stock fell 13.70%. The $108.9m / $512.7m / $403.7m pro-forma bridge is in the 2026-07-10 exhibit the hunter cites. Third parties have already published a full-year revenue model: S&P's 2026-08-12 downgrade note projects 'fiscal 2027 revenues near $400 million', i.e. exactly the guide midpoint, and the quoted Q2 consensus of $99.0m against a Q2 FY26 TDS base of $101m already embeds ~2.7 of the claimed 4 points of inflection. Management also publicly pre-explained the back-half shape on 2026-06-09 (labour-based professional-services and coaching revenue 'shifting to periods later in this fiscal year', FCF resuming in Q4), so the required trajectory is stated guidance, not a hidden implication. What is genuinely undrawn is only the crisp subtraction that Q2-Q4 must run -0.7% against a Q1 running -4.7%; I could find no article stating that number. That residual, plus the fact that the recent 29% drawdown is traceable to credit rather than to revenue trend, is why this is not in the 80s.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Skillsoft's Q4 FY26 8-K sets FY27 TDS-only guidance of $388-406m revenue and $108-116m adjusted EBITDA against FY26 TDS revenue of $403.7m -- the flat-bracketing comparison in the finding, published five months before this print.
Q1 FY27 continuing revenue of $94.5m, down 4.7% YoY, with FY27 guidance of $388-406m reaffirmed and GK reclassified to discontinued operations as of 2026-04-30.
Wire coverage headlines the $388-406m FY27 revenue outlook alongside the divestiture and refinancing focus.

Management discloses the 21% consumer decline, the government-bookings headwind with a 12-15 month absorption cycle, and that labour-based revenue expected in H1 shifts to later in the fiscal year -- i.e. management itself guided the back-half weighting the finding treats as an unflagged requirement.
Pro forma exhibit gives FY26 total revenue $512.7m, GK discontinued revenue ~$108.9m and continuing-operations revenue $403.7m -- the exact bridge the finding computes.
S&P's downgrade note publishes its own FY27 forecast of revenue 'near $400 million' post-divestiture, an independent third party modelling the same roughly-flat continuing-revenue year.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Two of the last three prints were double-digit down (-12.02% on 2026-04-07 when this guide was issued, -13.70% on 2026-06-09 when it was reaffirmed against a -4.7% Q1), and the stock sits 62.8% below its 52-week high at $6.66. The market has repeatedly repriced this exact guide downward on the exact dates it was published. Against that, the 20-day -29% has an identifiable non-revenue cause (S&P downgrade 2026-08-12, board resignation 8-K 2026-08-27), so the drawdown is not itself evidence that the revenue-inflection point specifically is in -- which caps this in the 50s rather than the 70s. No option chain, so no skew read available.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that no sell-side model or published note has the FY27 revenue bridge -- or a Q2 consensus materially above $101m, which would show the Street had not even absorbed the Q1 run-rate.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The load-bearing facts are both published and one of them is wire-level: Kisling's appointment effective 2026-05-20 and Frederick's retirement were announced in an 8-K filed 2026-05-21, and Kisling was already on the 2026-06-09 call speaking to the reaffirmed guidance. The 'new CFO's first owned quarter, therefore reset risk' heuristic is one of the most widely rehearsed setups in earnings analysis and is age, not novelty. What the hunter adds is the Frederick advisory-expiry date of 2026-09-04, which is genuinely obscure -- it is a clause in the 2026-05-21 8-K body and I found no article, note or screen that connects it to tonight's print -- so this is not a high number. But obscurity is doing all the work: the mechanism is weak. A retiring CFO's advisory contract lapsing on a routine ~3.5-month schedule confers no authority over guidance and did not restrain Kisling on 2026-06-09, when he had been in the chair twenty days and reaffirmed the range anyway. The date coincidence is decorative; the real content is the generic reset-risk trope, and that is thoroughly known. Note too that Kisling co-owns the guide already, having publicly reaffirmed it, which cuts directly against the clean-slate framing.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Kisling appointed CFO effective 2026-05-20; Frederick retired as CFO and agreed to serve as an Advisor through 2026-09-04 with continued salary, vesting and a $125,000 retention bonus.
Kisling appears on the Q1 FY27 call as CFO, reaffirms the FY27 guidance and states his priorities -- so the incoming CFO has already publicly endorsed the inherited number.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move is attributable to the 2026-05-21 CFO 8-K that I can isolate; the 20-day window (from roughly 2026-08-11) does not contain it, and the one management-related 8-K inside the window is the 2026-08-27 item 5.02 board resignation of Helena Foulkes, a different event. So the specific advisory-expiry fact has no visible price footprint -- which is the honest case for a lower number. The offsetting evidence is the reaction history: three of the last four prints fell 12-21.5%, so the market already assigns high probability to a bad guidance outcome regardless of who signs it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A concrete precedent at this company, or a disclosure tying Frederick's release-of-claims to guidance authority, that made the 2026-09-04 expiry mechanically rather than rhetorically relevant.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both legs are ordinary, heavily covered public earnings events from listed companies with real analyst followings, reported on their scheduled dates and picked up across Investing.com, GuruFocus, Yahoo and the wires within hours. Docebo's 2026-08-07 print -- ARR $255.1m, +9.5% YoY, second consecutive quarter of re-acceleration, FY guidance lifted $3.5m -- was covered as a beat-and-raise with a transcript headline reading 'lifts outlook'; Coursera's 2026-07-29 enterprise NRR was reported the same way. Nothing here is unpublished; the only step the hunter takes is the read-across to Skillsoft, which is the standard sector exercise any generalist performs and which multiple outlets already frame as 'enterprise L&D demand'. It is also self-cancelling on its own terms: the finding states the two comps disagree, then privileges the favourable one on a similarity judgement that is contestable -- Docebo is a mid-market LMS platform re-accelerating partly on acquisitions and an OEM base, while Skillsoft's decline is driven by government contract losses absorbed over a 12-15 month cycle and a 21% consumer decline, neither of which Docebo has any exposure to. A read-across whose direction depends on which comp you choose is not information.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Docebo's Q2 2026 release: ARR of US$255.1m at 2026-06-30, +9.5% YoY, revenue $68.7m +13%, with revised FY2026 guidance.
Same-day wire coverage of Docebo beating Q2 estimates and lifting its outlook, including the $3.5m guidance raise decomposition.
Coverage headlining the ARR re-acceleration and raised full-year guidance.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: SKIL fell about 29% over the twenty sessions that begin roughly 2026-08-11, i.e. immediately after the Docebo print. Whatever the market did with the enterprise-learning read-across, it did not bid SKIL on it -- the tape ran the other way over precisely this window, which is consistent with the read-across being seen and dismissed as irrelevant to a levered, government-exposed content business. Run-up 5d is +1.99%, no reversal into the print.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A specific overlap -- shared named enterprise accounts, or a Docebo disclosure about content-subscription renewals -- that made the read-across mechanical rather than thematic.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The refinancing question is not merely known here, it is the dominant published narrative on this name and it demonstrably moved the price inside the very drawdown the brief asks me to account for. On 2026-08-12 S&P downgraded Skillsoft to 'CCC+' from 'B-' with a negative outlook, explicitly on 'high leverage and refinancing risk ahead of the company's 2028 debt maturity', publishing the liquidity numbers ($115m cash, $75m AR facility), the ~7x leverage path, and the warning that it could cut further if the potential for a distressed transaction rises. That is the single largest published event in the 20-session window and gives the -29% a specific, refinancing-shaped cause. Upstream of it, Hovsepian's 'top management priority' language and Kisling's 'addressing our upcoming debt maturities' are both in the 2026-06-09 transcript, the Seeking Alpha wire headline for that call literally names debt refinancing, and the GK close on 2026-07-06 was filed 2026-07-10. So 'a refinancing update is due tonight and matters enormously to a $57m equity stub sitting under ~$580m of term debt' is the consensus frame, not an edge. What survives is only that the content of tonight's statement is unknown -- but that is an option-payoff assertion, not information, and the asymmetry claim is contestable in both directions: after an August downgrade that named distressed-exchange risk, silence or a hint at a liability-management exercise is not cheap, it is the outcome the credit market is already braced for. The finding's own numbers are also slightly stale: the 10-Q puts initial term loans at $580.2m at 2026-04-30, not $574.6m.

prior_publication.what_it_says: S&P downgrades Skillsoft to CCC+ from B- with negative outlook explicitly on refinancing risk ahead of the 2028 maturity, flagging possible distressed transaction or conventional default over the next twelve months.

Hovsepian: 'Once the GK transaction closes, refinancing our debt will be a top management priority'; Kisling names addressing upcoming maturities as the top financial priority; gross debt stated at $576m, net $457m.
Wire headline for the June call names the divestiture and debt refinancing as the focus -- the setup is literally in the wire copy.
8-K reporting completion of the Global Knowledge sale to an affiliate of Enduring Ventures on 2026-07-06 -- the trigger condition the finding relies on, publicly filed two months ago.
10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-04-30 disclosing initial term loans outstanding of $580.2m at SOFR + 5.25% maturing 2028-07-16.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 20-session window opens around 2026-08-11 and the S&P downgrade lands 2026-08-12, one day in -- the -29.22% run-up figure is, on the available record, substantially a repricing of exactly this refinancing risk. That is the strongest available demonstration that the topic is in the price rather than beside it. Realised vol of 68.3% annualised and a $6.66 spot against ~$580m of debt confirm the equity is trading as an option on the refinancing, which is precisely what 'already priced' looks like on a levered stub. No option chain, so no skew corroboration either way; 44,231 average shares a day (~$295k of turnover) means anything discovered here is close to untradeable at size regardless.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that a specific, non-obvious refinancing structure (a named amend-and-extend, an equitisation, a sponsor injection) is already agreed and disclosable tonight, rather than the generic expectation of commentary.

interactions: Three couplings worth recording. (1) Findings #0 and #3 rest on the same SEC accession, 0001437749-26-023329 filed 2026-07-10: #0 uses its pro forma exhibit ex_981295.htm for the $512.7m / $108.9m / $403.7m bridge and #3 uses the 8-K body skil20260624_8k.htm for the 2026-07-06 GK close. One filing, two findings -- counting both at full weight double-counts a single public document that the market saw two months ago. (2) #0 and #2 point opposite ways on the same variable. #0 argues Q2-Q4 continuing revenue must inflect four points and implicitly will not; #2 argues the enterprise-learning read-across is positive. They cannot both be edge on tonight's revenue line, and any aggregation that sums their impacts without netting is claiming information from a contradiction. (3) #1 and #3 are two readings of the same management-transition complex around the 2026-06-09 call: #1 reads Kisling's first owned quarter as reset/kitchen-sink risk (bearish), #3 reads the same call's refinancing pledge as a source of positive asymmetry (bullish). They are near-mirrors and should not both score. Separately, #0's arithmetic is correct -- I verified $403.7m pro forma continuing revenue, Q1 FY27 $94.5m and Q2 FY26 TDS $101m independently -- but the quoted Q2 consensus of ~$99.0m already contains most of the inflection the finding treats as unrecognised, which weakens #0 and #1 together, since both depend on the Street not having absorbed the Q1 run-rate.
